issues.description: ExcellenceLand constructor parameter order: The UML in the problem statement (class ExcellenceLand) lists two attributes in this order: 1) excellencyLevel : double, 2) excellentEnough : boolean. The task text (Tasks, task 3) additionally requires a private attribute rides of type List<Ride> but does not state where it should appear in the attribute order. The solution implementation defines the constructor as ExcellenceLand(List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel), i.e. parameters in the order (rides, excellentEnough, excellencyLevel). This conflicts with the UML ordering for the two named attributes and leaves the position of the added rides attribute ambiguous. Students following the UML order or an alternative ordering may implement a different constructor parameter order than the tests/solution expect, causing compilation/test mismatches and confusion about the canonical parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected constructor parameter order explicit and consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferable): Update the UML and problem text to include the rides attribute in the intended position so the UML shows the final attribute order (for example: if intended order is rides, excellentEnough, excellencyLevel, add '-rides: List<Ride>' in that place). Then update template code and tests to use that same constructor signature. Option B: Change the constructor in template and solution to follow the UML-listed order for the existing attributes and then append rides in a clearly defined position (for example (double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides)), and update the problem text/tests to state this explicit parameter order. Ensure template, tests, and solution all use the same parameter order so students have an unambiguous target.
